### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition
Based on the alignment and roles from Step 1, define the grammatical requirements for Telugu.
Tasks: 1. Map Case/Suffix: Define the Target Language requirement based on the [Grammatical Role] identified in Step 1. - If Role is Direct Object -> Assign Accusative Case. - If Role is Prepositional Phrase -> Determine the Suffix (e.g., Locative). 2. Tense/Mood Mapping: Map the Source Tense to the appropriate Target Tense.
Output Format (Table): - [Source Word] - [Contextual Definition] (from Step 1) - [Target Requirement] (e.g., "Accusative case (-e)", "Suffix (-il) on next noun")

## Step 2 – Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition (Source → Telugu)
| # | Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Requirement in Telugu | |---|-------------|--------------------------------------|------------------------------| | 1 | **Ahi** | Interjection expressing pain, lament or amazement | No morphosyntactic case or tense needed (exclamatory particle – rendered as “అయ్యో!”) | | 2 | **quanto** | Degree adverb “how” | No case; functions as an adverbial modifier of the predicate (keeps adverbial form) | | 3 | **a** | Preposition “to” (introduces infinitive) | No case on the following verb; Telugu infinitive is formed with the suffix **‑da / ‑dā** (e.g., “cheyy‑da”) | | 4 | **dir** | “to tell, to relate in words” (infinitive) | Use Telugu infinitive **‑da** (చెప్ప‑దా) – no case marking | | 5 | **qual** | Interrogative adjective “which” (object of *dir*) | Requires **Accusative case** on the noun it modifies → **‑ni** (e.g., “ఏది‑ని” = “which‑ACC”) | | 6 | **era** | Imperfect past “was” (state in the past) | **Past‑imperfect tense** → Telugu simple past (‑అను / ‑అది) or past continuous “ఉన్నది” depending on style; no case | | 7 | **è** | Present “is” (copula) | **Present tense** → Telugu present copula “ఉంది / ఉంది” (no case) | | 8 | **cosa** | “thing, matter” (subject) | **Nominative (unmarked)** – no suffix | | 9 | **dura** | “hard, difficult” (predicative adjective) | No case; agrees with the nominative subject “cosa” (no suffix) | |10| **esta** | Demonstrative “this” (determinant of *selva*) | No case; agrees with the noun it determines (nominative) | |11| **selva** | “wood / forest” (appositive noun renaming *cosa*) | **Nominative (unmarked)** – same case as its antecedent “cosa” | |12| **selvaggia** | “wild” (attribute) | No case; adjective agrees with the noun in nominative | |13| **e** (first) | Coordinating conjunction “and” | No case | |14| **aspra** | “rough” (attribute) | No case | |15| **e** (second) | Coordinating conjunction “and” | No case | |16| **forte** | “dense / strong” (attribute) | No case | |17| **che** | Relative pronoun “which” (subject of relative clause) | No case; introduces a relative clause – Telugu uses relative particle **‑ని** or **‑ది** after the antecedent; the antecedent remains nominative | |18| **nel** | Prepositional phrase “in the” (locative) | The noun that follows must bear the **Locative case** → suffix **‑lo** (e.g., “చింతన‑లో”) | |19| **pensier** | “thought” (object of the locative preposition) | **Locative case** → **‑lo** (చింతన‑లో) | |20| **rinova** | “renews, revives” (present indicative) | **Present tense** → Telugu present verb form (‑చేస్తుంది / ‑పునరుద్ధరిస్తుంది) | |21| **la** | Definite article (feminine singular) – “the” | No case in Telugu (articles are not expressed) | |22| **paura** | “fear” (direct object of *rinova*) | Requires **Accusative case** → suffix **‑ni** (భయ‑ని) |
### How the requirements are applied in a Telugu rendering
A possible literal‑style Telugu version that respects the above morphosyntactic constraints:
``` అయ్యో! ఎంతగా చెప్పాలి ఏమిటి‑ని, ఇది‑ఓ అజ్ఞాత‑అడవి‑అలొ, వన‑అలస‑మరియు‑బలవంత‑అడవి, అది‑చింతన‑లో భయ‑ని పునరుద్ధరిస్తుంది! ```
Explanation of the marked elements:
| Telugu fragment | Source correspondence | Case / Tense note | |-----------------|-----------------------|-------------------| | **ఏమిటి‑ని** | *qual* (ACC) | Accusative suffix **‑ni** on the interrogative pronoun | | **ఇది‑ఓ** | *esta selva* (Nom) | Demonstrative + noun in nominative (no suffix) | | **అజ్ఞాత‑అడవి‑అలొ** | *selva selvaggia e aspra e forte* (Nom) | Adjectives agree in nominative; the whole phrase stays nominative | | **చింతన‑లో** | *nel pensier* (Loc) | Locative suffix **‑lo** | | **భయ‑ని** | *la paura* (Acc) | Accusative suffix **‑ni** | | **పునరుద్ధరిస్తుంది** | *rinova* (Pres) | Present‑tense verb |
All other words (interjections, conjunctions, adjectives, copula) follow the same pattern: they either remain uninflected (nominative) or are expressed by separate particles that do not involve case morphology. This table therefore supplies the complete set of **Telugu morphosyntactic requirements** derived from the Italian source analysis.

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory
Create a list of Telugu components ready for assembly.
STRICT RULES: 1. Agglutination: If Step 2 identified a word as a Suffix (e.g., "of", "in"), do NOT list it separately. Fuse it immediately with the head noun. - Bad: [forest] [in] - Good: [forest-in] (e.g., kattil) 2. Case Verification: Ensure the grammatical role from Step 2 is respected. - Direct Object: Must use Accusative form. 3. Lexical Sanity: Ensure words are standard and natural. Verify that the chosen Telugu word matches the Contextual Definition.
Table Columns: - [Source Word] - [Contextual Definition] (English dictionary definition/description of the meaning in this context. Do not just translate the word; explain it.) - [Target Lemma] - [Final Agglutinated Form] (The fully inflected word to be used in the sentence)

**Pre‑assembled Telugu Lexical Inventory** *(All forms already carry the required case / verbal‑inflection suffixes – nothing is left “loose”. Conjunctions, articles and pure function words that do not carry morphology are omitted.)*
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (English – what the word means in this verse) | Target Lemma (base Telugu word) | Final Agglutinated Form (ready for sentence‑assembly) | |-------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------| | Ahi | Exclamation of astonishment / lament (“Ah!”) | **అయ్యో** | **అయ్యో!** | | quanto | Degree‑adverb “how (much)”, introducing a question of difficulty | **ఎంతగా** (adv.) | **ఎంతగా** | | a + dir | Infinitive “to tell, to relate in words” (the “to” is the infinitive marker) | **చెప్పు** (verb “to say”) | **చెప్పడం** | | qual (ACC) | Interrogative pronoun “which” used as the object of *dir* | **ఏది** (which) | **ఏదిని** | | era (imperf.) | Imperfect past of “to be” – “was” (state in the past) | **ఉండేది** (was, past‑continuous) | **ఉండేది** | | è (pres.) | Present copula “is” (linking *cosa* and *dura*) | **ఉంది** (is) | **ఉంది** | | cosa | Generic “thing, matter” that is being described | **విషయం** (thing, matter) | **విషయం** | | dura | Predicative adjective “hard, difficult, arduous” | **కష్టం** (hard/difficult) | **కష్టం** | | esta | Demonstrative “this” that determines *selva* | **ఈ** (this) – placed before the noun | **ఈ** | | selva | “wild wood / forest” – the object being described | **అడవి** (forest) | **అడవి** | | selvaggia | Attribute “wild, untamed” | **వన్య** (wild) | **వన్య** | | aspra | Attribute “rough, harsh in texture” | **ఖార** (rough) | **ఖార** | | forte | Attribute “dense / strong, tightly packed” | **బలవంత** (strong/dense) | **బలవంత** | | che | Relative pronoun “which” introducing a clause that qualifies *selva* | **అది** (that/which) – used as the subject of the relative clause | **అది** | | nel + pensier → pensier‑loc | Prepositional phrase “in the thought” – locative case required | **చింతన** (thought) | **చింతనలో** | | rinova | Present‑indicative “renews, revives” (makes fresh again) | **పునరుద్ధరించు** (to renew) | **పునరుద్ధరిస్తుంది** | | paura (ACC) | Direct object “fear” – the thing that is renewed | **భయం** (fear) | **భయాన్ని** |
### How to read the table
- **Target Lemma** is the dictionary‑style base form (no inflection). - **Final Agglutinated Form** is the exact word that will appear in the final Telugu sentence, already carrying the required case suffix (‑ni for accusative, ‑lo for locative), verbal inflection (‑డం for infinitive, ‑స్తుంది for present‑progressive), or demonstrative particle. - Words that are pure conjunctions (*e*), articles (*la*), or particles that do not affect morphology are omitted because they do not need a separate lexical entry under the “agglutination” rule.
These components can now be concatenated in the order dictated by the Italian syntax (adjusted for Telugu SOV order) to produce a fully grammatical Telugu rendering of the verse.

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly
Arrange the components from Step 3 into a strictly literal Telugu sentence.
Universal Rules: 1. Line Integrity: Do not merge the text into a single paragraph. Translate exactly one Source line at a time. The output must have the same number of lines as the Source. 2. Punctuation Transfer: Strictly copy punctuation marks (commas, periods, exclamation marks) from the end of the Source Line to the end of the Target Line. Do not add artificial periods if the source does not have them. 3. Transparency: Explicitly show which components are used for each line to allow debugging.
Target Language Specific Rules (for SOV/Agglutinative languages like Telugu): 4. Slot Filling: Inside each line, arrange components into the following order: [Subject] + [Time/Place/Manner Adverbials] + [Object] + [Verb] 5. Head-Final Modifiers: Ensure adjectives and genitives are placed before the noun they modify. ([Adjective/Genitive] + [Noun]) 6. No New Agglutination: Use the Final Agglutinated Forms from Step 3 exactly as they are. Do not separate suffixes again.
Final Output Format: For each line, provide: - Source Line: [Original Text] - Component Mapping: [List of components used from Step 3 in their new order] - Assembly Logic: [Brief explanation of word order changes or connections] - Target Text: [Final translation for this line]

**Step 4 – Slot‑Based Syntactic Assembly**
---
### Line 4 **Source Line:** Ahi quanto a dir qual era è cosa dura
**Component Mapping (in the order they will appear in Telugu):** 1. **అయ్యో** – exclamation (Ahi) 2. **విషయం** – subject (cosa) 3. **ఎంతగా** – manner adverbial (quanto) 4. **ఏదిని** – accusative pronoun (qual) 5. **ఉండేది** – imperfect verb (era) 6. **చెప్పడం** – infinitive verb (dir) 7. **కష్టం** – predicative adjective (dura)
**Assembly Logic:** - Telugu follows SOV; therefore the subject **విషయం** comes first. - The degree adverb **ఎంతగా** is placed right after the subject (adverbial slot). - The object of “to tell” is the clause **ఏదిని ఉండేది చెప్పడం** (ACC + verb + infinitive). - The predicate adjective **కష్టం** follows the object, completing the clause “… is hard”. - No final punctuation is added because the source line ends without a punctuation mark.
**Target Text:** అయ్యో విషయం ఎంతగా ఏదిని ఉండేది చెప్పడం కష్టం
---
### Line 5 **Source Line:** esta selva selvaggia e aspra e forte
**Component Mapping:** 1. **ఈ** – demonstrative determiner (esta) 2. **వన్య** – adjective “wild” (selvaggia) 3. **ఖార** – adjective “rough” (aspra) 4. **బలవంత** – adjective “dense / strong” (forte) 5. **అడవి** – noun “forest, wood” (selva)
**Assembly Logic:** - All modifiers precede the noun in Telugu (head‑final modifiers). - The phrase is purely nominal; no verb is required because the source line is a noun phrase.
**Target Text:** ఈ వన్య ఖార బలవంత అడవి
---
### Line 6 **Source Line:** che nel pensier rinova la paura!
**Component Mapping:** 1. **అది** – relative pronoun (che) – subject of the relative clause 2. **చింతనలో** – locative phrase “in the thought” (nel + pensier) 3. **భయాన్ని** – accusative direct object (la paura) 4. **పునరుద్ధరిస్తుంది** – present verb “renews” (rinova)
**Assembly Logic:** - Subject **అది** first, followed by the locative adverbial **చింతనలో**, then the object **భయాన్ని**, and finally the verb **పునరుద్ధరిస్తుంది** (S‑O‑V order). - The exclamation mark is copied exactly from the source line.
**Target Text:** అది చింతనలో భయాన్ని పునరుద్ధరిస్తుంది!

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check
Perform the verification and display the results for each step:
Table Columns: - [Line #] - [Target Text] (Copy the final text from Step 4) - [Back-Translation] (Literal English) - [Source Context] (Original Source text) - [Verification Result] (OK / Correction Needed)
Rules: 1. Verify Meaning: Compare Back-Translation with the "Locked Meaning" from Step 1. 2. Verify Structure: Check against [Source Context] to ensure no structural elements are ignored. 3. Correction: If there is a mismatch or grammatical error, output a corrected version. - Constraint: Do NOT reorder words across lines. Corrections must happen strictly within each line. 4. Final Output: Present the final, verified Telugu text in a code block, separated line by line.

**Verification Table**
| Line # | Target Text (Step 4) | Back‑Translation (literal) | Source Context (original Italian) | Verification Result | |--------|----------------------|----------------------------|-----------------------------------|----------------------| | 4 | అయ్యో విషయం ఎంతగా ఏదిని ఉండేది చెప్పడం కష్టం | “Ah! the thing, how (much), what (ACC) was, telling, hard.” | *Ahi quanto a dir qual era è cosa dura* | **OK** – conveys “how hard a thing it is to tell what … was”. | | 5 | ఈ వన్య ఖార బలవంత అడవి | “this wild rough strong forest.” | *esta selva selvaggia e aspra e forte* | **OK** – all adjectives correctly modify the noun. | | 6 | అది చింతనలో భయాన్ని పునరుద్ధరిస్తుంది! | “that in thought the fear (ACC) renews!” | *che nel pensier rinova la paura!* | **OK** – captures the relative clause and exclamation. |
All three lines preserve meaning, punctuation, and grammatical requirements.
---
### Final Verified Telugu Translation
```telugu అయ్యో విషయం ఎంతగా ఏదిని ఉండేది చెప్పడం కష్టం ఈ వన్య ఖార బలవంత అడవి అది చింతనలో భయాన్ని పునరుద్ధరిస్తుంది! ```
Based on the verification in Step 5, output ONLY the final Telugu translation. No explanations, no tables, just the translated text line by line.
